data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment
* **code_version:** $(git rev-parse HEAD)

### 2. Incident Overview
**Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker

#### Expected Behavior
aws-setup-bucket.sh preflight_iam should verify the caller has the 5 required S3 actions (s3:CreateBucket, s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock, s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration, s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration, s3:PutBucketPolicy) and proceed when all return EvalDecision=allowed.

#### Actual Behavior
Line 101: `_aws iam list-attached-user-policies --output json` — AWS CLI requires `--user-name` argument. Without it, the call fails with `ParamValidation: the following arguments are required: --user-name`. The script's parse falls through to `policy_count=0`, triggering "ERROR: Missing required IAM permissions" + exit 5.

Verified: running user joeoakhart has AdministratorAccess attached AND simulate-principal-policy returns "allowed" for all 5 required actions. Yet aws-setup-bucket.sh exits 5.

Impact: blocks 73d7-1968 (live e2e self-use validation) closure. AWS infrastructure cannot be provisioned via the documented setup sequence.

#### Suggested Fix
Replace lines 99–119 with `aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn $(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Arn --output text) --action-names s3:CreateBucket s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration s3:PutBucketPolicy` and assert each EvalDecision=allowed. This matches the sibling pattern already in aws-setup-lambda.sh:152 and aws-verify-live.sh:242.
data.title: [aws-setup-bucket.sh]: preflight_iam uses list-attached-user-policies without --user-name -> ParamValidation error masks IAM permissions as missing
